name: FL-01
label: Safe R

key_factors: Patronis's massive fundraising and outside-spending advantage
Markets price Valimont's chances at roughly 4%
No public polling of the race
model.rationale: The R+18 district, Patronis's incumbency, and a 20-to-1 fundraising edge leave Valimont with no evident path; prediction markets agree at about 4%. The forecast stays essentially at the fundamentals, with slight widening for the incumbent's resource advantage.
model.watch: Any unexpected scandal or late polling showing a single-digit race would be the main signal to revisit.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Florida's 1st District is one of the most Republican seats in the state, with a partisan lean of R+18. Incumbent Jimmy Patronis, who won the seat in a special election, is running for a full term and holds a decisive financial advantage: he has raised nearly $3.8 million and benefits from over $2 million in outside support, while Democrat Gay Valimont has raised about $174,000 with modest outside help and no opposition spending against Patronis.

No public polls cover the race, and no expert raters have flagged it as competitive. Prediction markets give Valimont roughly a 4% chance of winning. With the fundamentals, money, and market pricing all pointing the same direction, the seat is rated Safe Republican, with Patronis favored by roughly 18 points.
